## Context / Problem

Discovered from nonblack-brigandish-guillemot: its closing plan review raised this as an advisory finding. After ADR 0125, rebar checks op-certs for validity only unless the verifying environment lists the keys it trusts in `verify.trusted_opcert_keys`. ADR 0125 says that list belongs to each environment's own configuration, not the repository.

Nothing enforces that. `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` is an ordinary `[verify]` key (`src/rebar/_config_sections.py:83`). No code restricts which config layer may set it; a search of `src/rebar/_config*.py` finds no repository-scope restriction for any key. The op-cert gate resolves its configuration through the repository root, so a committed `rebar.toml` that sets the key is read like any other layer. A change under review could add a key to that file and widen the trust list of the very gate that checks it.

## Approach (operator decision, 2026-11-20)

CI resolves the op-cert gate's trust configuration from main's `rebar.toml`, never from the `rebar.toml` in the change under review. A change can then edit `rebar.toml` freely, but its edit only takes effect for gating after it has itself merged through review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The CI op-cert gate reads `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` from main's `rebar.toml`, not the change's.
- [ ] A change that adds a key to `rebar.toml` does not widen the trust list its own gate run uses, shown by a test that tries it.
- [ ] No config key, env var or flag is added by the fix.
